Two Factor Confirmatory Factor Analysis Model

Source: R/cfa_2.R
cfa_2.Rd

Fits a two factor confirmatory factor analysis model to raw item data or a sample covariance matrix. This is the two factor special case of fa_confirmatory: the function is a convenience wrapper that only requires the items of each factor, builds the two factor specification, and forwards everything else to fa_confirmatory(). The factors are named f1 and f2, so the rows of the returned table are lambda_f1_1, lambda_f2_1, phi_f1_f2 (the factor correlation), omega_f1, omega_f2, and so on, exactly as a two factor fa_confirmatory() call would report them (the syntax column names the item behind each number). To name the factors substantively, or for three or more factors, call fa_confirmatory directly.

Usage

cfa_2(
  data = NULL,
  factor_1,
  factor_2,
  S = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  equal_loading = FALSE,
  equal_error = FALSE,
  correlated_factors = TRUE,
  estimator = "ML",
  missing = "fiml",
  se = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  output = c("verbose", "measurement", "summary", "standardized", "fit"),
  ...,
  wald_df = Inf,
  rmsea_conf_level = 0.9
)

Arguments

data

A raw data matrix or data frame, rows are respondents and columns include the items named in factor_1 and factor_2. Supply exactly one of data or S.

factor_1

Character vector naming the items of the first factor (two or more).

factor_2

Character vector naming the items of the second factor (two or more). No item may appear in both factors. An item of either factor that is not a column of data or an item of S is refused with an error of class dmar_items_invalid (see dmar_metadata).

S

A symmetric covariance matrix of the items, with dimnames naming the items; N is then required. Supply exactly one of data or S.

N

Total sample size. Required with S; ignored (inferred from the rows) with data.

equal_loading

Logical, or a named logical vector with one element per factor. TRUE constrains the loadings within a factor to a single value (across factors nothing is equated). Defaults to FALSE.

equal_error

Logical, or a named logical vector with one element per factor. TRUE constrains the error variances within a factor to a single value. Defaults to FALSE.

correlated_factors

Logical. If TRUE (default) the factors covary freely; because each factor variance is fixed to 1, the phi terms for factor pairs are the latent correlations. If FALSE the factor covariances are fixed to zero.

estimator

Character; estimator passed to lavaan. Must be one of "ML" (default; maximum likelihood, fully efficient under multivariate normality), "MLR" (robust maximum likelihood, raw data required: maximum likelihood estimates with the test statistic corrected for nonnormality, the scaled statistic of Satorra and Bentler, 1994, in the form Yuan and Bentler, 2000, gave it for incomplete data; its matching Huber-White sandwich standard errors are used when se is omitted), "WLS" (the asymptotic distribution free estimator of Browne, 1984; raw data and a large sample required), "WLSMV" (diagonally weighted least squares with mean- and variance-adjusted test statistic; Muthén, 1984; Muthén, du Toit, & Spisic, 1997; the standard choice for ordered categorical items, and what ordered switches to), or "GLS" (generalized least squares; Browne, 1974). With a robust estimator the reported fit indices are the robust versions.

missing

Character; missing-data handling when raw data are supplied: "fiml" (default; full information maximum likelihood, which uses every case with an observed item; lavaan's name "ml" is accepted), "listwise" (listwise deletion), "pairwise" (passed to lavaan, for ordered items), "two_stage" (two-stage maximum likelihood with normal theory standard errors and test), or "robust_two_stage" (two-stage maximum likelihood with standard errors and test robust to nonnormality); lavaan's spellings "two.stage" and "robust.two.stage" are accepted for the last two. See Details for two-stage estimation. Ignored with S, except that a two-stage request with S is an error, since a covariance matrix has no incomplete cases. With ordered items, "ml"/"fiml" and the two-stage options are not available; use "pairwise" or "listwise". FIML needs a maximum likelihood estimator of continuous items with normal theory or Huber-White standard errors. When the default meets ordered items, a least squares estimator ("WLS", "WLSMV", "GLS"), se = "robust.sem", or a Satorra-Bentler kind of test passed through ..., the items are fitted as they stand if no item value is missing (listwise deletion then deletes nothing), and otherwise the call stops and names the option to choose, rather than deleting cases unasked. With complete data FIML and listwise deletion give the same estimates and the same chi square, and for estimator = "ML" the same fit indices; the standard errors differ slightly, since FIML takes them from the observed information, as lavaan does and as Savalei (2010) recommends with incomplete data, and listwise deletion from the expected information.

se

Standard error method passed to lavaan. The default, NULL, follows the estimator: model-based "standard" errors for ML, GLS and WLS; Huber-White sandwich "robust.huber.white" errors for MLR; and "robust.sem" errors for WLSMV. Explicit compatible choices are retained. The ML and MLR point estimates use the same likelihood; their standard errors and tests use different reference assumptions. This difference does not depend on whether optimization is iterative or an equivalent solution is computed analytically. "robust.sem" requires complete data and is refused with FIML; use "robust.huber.white" to retain incomplete respondents. No standard-error request silently changes the missing-data treatment. "none" requests point estimates only. Under two-stage estimation the matching corrected two-stage errors are used; se must be NULL, "standard", or "none". MLR and Huber-White errors require raw data. Robust SEM errors from covariance input require ML and a matching NACOV in ....

conf_level

Confidence level for the parameter confidence intervals, including the delta method intervals for omega, AVE, and H. Defaults to 0.95. It does not reach the RMSEA interval, whose level is rmsea_conf_level.

output

Format of the returned object:

"verbose"

(default) Parameter estimates with confidence intervals, the per-factor defined parameters (loading_sum, error_sum, omega, ave, H), and fit information.

"measurement"

The measurement-property rows only: per factor omega, ave, and H (with delta method standard errors and confidence intervals), the latent correlation phi for every factor pair (with its confidence interval), and, for raw data, the heterotrait-monotrait ratio htmt for every factor pair via htmt.

"summary"

The raw summary() output from lavaan (not a data frame).

"standardized"

The standardized parameter estimates from lavaan::standardizedSolution(), whose defined rows describe the standardized items: omega there is the reliability of the unit-weighted sum of the standardized items, while ave and H do not depend on the metric of the items and equal the rows of the other tables. For a factor with equal_loading or equal_error these rows are computed from each item's own standardized loading and error variance (see The standardized solution under Details of fa_confirmatory). Under se = "none" the se, z, pvalue, ci.lower, and ci.upper columns are NA.

"fit"

The raw lavaan fit object. Escape hatch for direct lavaan access, including likelihood ratio tests between two fa_confirmatory() fits via lavaan::lavTestLRT().

...

Additional arguments forwarded to fa_confirmatory and, through it, to lavaan (for example ordered, equal_intercept, or M).

wald_df

The reference distribution of the Wald intervals and p-values of the parameter rows: Inf (the default), the normal distribution, which leaves lavaan's intervals and p-values as they are; a single positive number, the degrees of freedom of a t distribution for every parameter row, the intervals and p-values recomputed from the same estimates and standard errors; or "missing_information", von Hippel's (2016) degrees of freedom \(\max\{3, N(1 - \gamma_j) - 1\}\) for each loading, from its fraction of missing information \(\gamma_j\) (\(N - 1\) with complete data), with every other row left on the normal reference. A number applies to the tables of output = "verbose", "measurement", and "standardized", the keyword to that of "verbose" only (the "measurement" table has no loading), and either needs standard errors other than "none" and "bootstrap"; the keyword also needs the fits its calibration covers, maximum likelihood (estimator = "ML" or "MLR") of continuous items by FIML or with complete data, with normal theory or Huber-White standard errors. Anything else is an error that says why. It follows ..., so it must be named in full. See Details.

rmsea_conf_level

Confidence level of the RMSEA interval of the fit rows, which the rmsea_ci_level row records. Defaults to 0.90, the conventional level, whose limits decide the tests of close and not close fit at .05 (see sem_fit_measures); rmsea_conf_level = 0.95 gives a 95 percent interval. It sets the level in the table DMAR returns and in its glance(); output = "summary" returns the lavaan summary, which shows lavaan's 90 percent interval whatever this argument is.

Value

The value of the corresponding fa_confirmatory call: a data.frame (classes dmar_fa_confirmatory, dmar_tbl) with one row per parameter (estimate, se, test_statistic, p_value, ci_lower, ci_upper) followed by the fit rows, or the alternative shapes selected by output (see ?fa_confirmatory).

Details

Each factor is identified by fixing its variance to 1 and estimating every loading; each item loads on exactly one factor (simple structure). The factor correlation is estimated by default and correlated_factors = FALSE fixes it to zero. Per-factor constraint vectors use the factor names, for example equal_loading = c(f1 = TRUE, f2 = FALSE). A fit whose likelihood has no maximum (an error variance that runs off below zero while the likelihood is flat or still rising) stops with an error of class dmar_no_maximum that prints the lavaan code of the fit, as fa_confirmatory describes; there, bounds = "pos.var" (which ... also passes on from here) or a different model are the choices.

References

Browne, M. W. (1974). Generalized least squares estimators in the analysis of covariance structures. South African Statistical Journal, 8, 1–24.

Browne, M. W. (1984). Asymptotically distribution-free methods for the analysis of covariance structures. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 37(1), 62–83. doi:10.1111/j.2044-8317.1984.tb00789.x

Muthén, B. (1984). A general structural equation model with dichotomous, ordered categorical, and continuous latent variable indicators. Psychometrika, 49(1), 115–132.

Muthén, B., du Toit, S. H. C., & Spisic, D. (1997). Robust inference using weighted least squares and quadratic estimating equations in latent variable modeling with categorical and continuous outcomes. Unpublished technical report.

Satorra, A., & Bentler, P. M. (1994). Corrections to test statistics and standard errors in covariance structure analysis. In A. von Eye & C. C. Clogg (Eds.), Latent variables analysis: Applications for developmental research (pp. 399–419). Thousand Oaks, CA: Sage.

Savalei, V. (2010). Expected versus observed information in SEM with incomplete normal and nonnormal data. Psychological Methods, 15(4), 352–367. doi:10.1037/a0020143

von Hippel, P. T. (2016). New confidence intervals and bias comparisons show that maximum likelihood can beat multiple imputation in small samples. Structural Equation Modeling, 23(3), 422–437. doi:10.1080/10705511.2015.1047931

Yuan, K.-H., & Bentler, P. M. (2000). Three likelihood-based methods for mean and covariance structure analysis with nonnormal missing data. Sociological Methodology, 30, 165–200.

See also

fa_confirmatory for the general function this wraps; cfa_1 for the one factor wrapper; htmt and average_variance_extracted for the discriminant and convergent validity summaries the output = "measurement" table reports alongside omega.

Examples

data(holzinger_swineford)

# Two factors, each named by its items.
cfa_2(holzinger_swineford,
      factor_1 = c("t6_paragraph_comprehension", "t7_sentence",
                   "t9_word_meaning"),
      factor_2 = c("t20_deduction", "t22_problem_reasoning",
                   "t23_series_completion"))

#>   f1: congeneric (no equality constraints)
#>   f2: congeneric (no equality constraints)

#>  f1 =~ t7_sentence                                        lambda_f1_2

# factor correlation, and the htmt ratio.
cfa_2(holzinger_swineford,
      factor_1 = c("t6_paragraph_comprehension", "t7_sentence",
                   "t9_word_meaning"),
      factor_2 = c("t20_deduction", "t22_problem_reasoning",
                   "t23_series_completion"),
      output = "measurement")
